facts.value: 1870 to 1871, rejection of the Vatican Council's decree on papal infallibility. First congress at Munich, September 1871

citations.excerpt: the designation assumed by those members of the Roman Catholic Church who refused to accept the decrees of the Vatican Council of 1870 defining the dogma of papal infallibility
the first Old Catholic Congress was able to meet at Munich , 22-24 September, 1871.

facts.value: Accept the authority of the undivided Church and the decrees of the first seven general councils.

citations.excerpt: Old Catholicism sets up the authority of the undivided Church, and accepts the decrees of the first seven general councils—down to the second council of Nicaea (787)

facts.value_before_verify: Accept the first seven ecumenical councils and an episcopal church order, but not papal infallibility or centralized papal government.

facts.value: Catholics who entered into relations with the Jansenist Church of Utrecht.

citations.excerpt: In the same year the Old Catholics, as they now began to be termed, entered into relations with the historical little Jansenist Church of Utrecht.

facts.value_before_verify: Churches formed in Germany, Switzerland and elsewhere after 1870, which entered relations with the Jansenist Church of Utrecht and received bishops from it.
